```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  dpi = 150
)
```

```{r data-import, include=FALSE}
# Delete this chunk after merging with A's Rmd.
clean <- read.csv(
  file.path("data", "hotels_clean.csv"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

```{r variable-coding, include=FALSE}
model_data <- clean
model_data$hotel <- relevel(factor(model_data$hotel), ref = "City Hotel")
model_data$arrival_date_month <- factor(
  model_data$arrival_date_month,
  levels = month.name
)
model_data$meal <- relevel(factor(model_data$meal), ref = "BB")
model_data$market_segment <- relevel(
  factor(model_data$market_segment),
  ref = "Online TA"
)
model_data$customer_type <- relevel(
  factor(model_data$customer_type),
  ref = "Transient"
)
model_data$reserved_room_type <- relevel(
  factor(model_data$reserved_room_type),
  ref = "A"
)
model_data$is_repeated_guest <- relevel(
  factor(model_data$is_repeated_guest),
  ref = "No"
)
model_data$domestic <- relevel(
  factor(model_data$domestic),
  ref = "International"
)
```

# Preliminary model

```{r model, include=FALSE}
model <- lm(
  adr ~ lead_time * hotel +
    arrival_date_month +
    stays_in_weekend_nights +
    stays_in_week_nights +
    adults +
    children +
    meal +
    market_segment +
    customer_type +
    reserved_room_type +
    is_repeated_guest +
    total_of_special_requests +
    domestic,
  data = model_data
)

model_summary <- summary(model)
```

We fitted a preliminary multiple linear regression using `r format(nobs(model), big.mark = ",")` completed bookings. The model included 14 predictors and a lead-time-by-hotel interaction.

```{r model-table}
coefficient_matrix <- coef(model_summary)
confidence_intervals <- confint(model)

coefficient_table <- data.frame(
  Term = rownames(coefficient_matrix),
  Estimate = coefficient_matrix[, "Estimate"],
  SE = coefficient_matrix[, "Std. Error"],
  Lower_95_CI = confidence_intervals[, 1],
  Upper_95_CI = confidence_intervals[, 2],
  p_value = coefficient_matrix[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
  row.names = NULL
)

coefficient_table[, 2:5] <- round(coefficient_table[, 2:5], 3)
coefficient_table$p_value <- format.pval(
  coefficient_table$p_value,
  digits = 3,
  eps = 0.001
)

knitr::kable(
  coefficient_table,
  caption = "Preliminary model estimates with standard errors and 95% confidence intervals."
)
```

```{r main-results, include=FALSE}
model_estimates <- coef(model)
interaction_term <- "lead_time:hotelResort Hotel"

city_slope <- unname(model_estimates["lead_time"])
interaction_estimate <- unname(model_estimates[interaction_term])
resort_slope <- city_slope + interaction_estimate

city_ci <- confidence_intervals["lead_time", ]
interaction_ci <- confidence_intervals[interaction_term, ]
```

For the City Hotel, one additional day of lead time was associated with a `r abs(round(city_slope, 4))`-euro decrease in mean ADR (95% CI: `r round(city_ci[1], 4)`, `r round(city_ci[2], 4)`), holding the other predictors fixed. The lead-time-by-hotel interaction estimate was `r round(interaction_estimate, 4)` euros (95% CI: `r round(interaction_ci[1], 4)`, `r round(interaction_ci[2], 4)`). Therefore, the estimated lead-time slope for the Resort Hotel was `r round(resort_slope, 4)` euros per day. Longer lead times were associated with lower ADR at both hotels, but the negative association was weaker at the Resort Hotel. The interaction confidence interval did not contain zero, providing evidence that the lead-time slopes differed between the two hotels. This hotel-specific difference was consistent with Abrate et al. (2012), who found that inter-temporal hotel pricing varies with hotel and customer characteristics. The adjusted R-squared was `r round(model_summary$adj.r.squared, 4)`. These results describe conditional associations, not causal effects.

# Model conditions

```{r condition-response, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.5, fig.cap="Conditional mean response check."}
plot(
  fitted(model),
  model_data$adr,
  xlab = "Fitted ADR",
  ylab = "Observed ADR",
  main = "Observed vs fitted ADR",
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.3,
  col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.15)
)
abline(0, 1, col = "red")
```

```{r condition-predictors, fig.width=9, fig.height=9, fig.cap="Pairwise plots of the numerical predictors."}
numeric_predictors <- model_data[c(
  "lead_time",
  "stays_in_weekend_nights",
  "stays_in_week_nights",
  "adults",
  "children",
  "total_of_special_requests"
)]

pairs(
  numeric_predictors,
  labels = c(
    "Lead time", "Weekend nights", "Weekday nights",
    "Adults", "Children", "Special requests"
  ),
  pch = ".",
  col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.15)
)
```

The observed-versus-fitted plot shows systematic departures from the reference line. The pairwise plots do not show strong curved relationships among the numerical predictors, although several count predictors are discrete and concentrated at small values. Therefore, the conditional mean response condition is questionable, while the conditional mean predictor condition appears reasonable for the numerical predictors.

# Residual analysis

```{r residual-values, include=FALSE}
model_residuals <- residuals(model)
fitted_values <- fitted(model)
point_colour <- rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.15)
```

```{r residual-core, fig.width=12, fig.height=4, fig.cap="Residuals versus fitted ADR and lead time, and the normal Q-Q plot."}
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

plot(
  fitted_values,
  model_residuals,
  xlab = "Fitted ADR",
  ylab = "Residual",
  main = "Residuals vs fitted",
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.3,
  col = point_colour
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

plot(
  model_data$lead_time,
  model_residuals,
  xlab = "Lead time (days)",
  ylab = "Residual",
  main = "Residuals vs lead time",
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.3,
  col = point_colour
)
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

qqnorm(
  model_residuals,
  main = "Normal Q-Q",
  pch = 16,
  cex = 0.3,
  col = point_colour
)
qqline(model_residuals, col = "red")

par(old_par)
```

```{r residual-numeric-1, fig.width=12, fig.height=4, fig.cap="Residuals versus weekend nights, weekday nights, and adults."}
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

plot(model_data$stays_in_weekend_nights, model_residuals,
     xlab = "Weekend nights", ylab = "Residual",
     main = "Residuals vs weekend nights", pch = 16, cex = 0.3,
     col = point_colour)
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

plot(model_data$stays_in_week_nights, model_residuals,
     xlab = "Weekday nights", ylab = "Residual",
     main = "Residuals vs weekday nights", pch = 16, cex = 0.3,
     col = point_colour)
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

plot(model_data$adults, model_residuals,
     xlab = "Adults", ylab = "Residual",
     main = "Residuals vs adults", pch = 16, cex = 0.3,
     col = point_colour)
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

par(old_par)
```

```{r residual-numeric-2, fig.width=12, fig.height=4, fig.cap="Residuals versus children and special requests, and by hotel."}
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

plot(model_data$children, model_residuals,
     xlab = "Children", ylab = "Residual",
     main = "Residuals vs children", pch = 16, cex = 0.3,
     col = point_colour)
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

plot(model_data$total_of_special_requests, model_residuals,
     xlab = "Special requests", ylab = "Residual",
     main = "Residuals vs special requests", pch = 16, cex = 0.3,
     col = point_colour)
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

boxplot(model_residuals ~ model_data$hotel,
        xlab = "Hotel", ylab = "Residual",
        main = "Residuals by hotel")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

par(old_par)
```

```{r residual-categorical-1, fig.width=12, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap="Residuals by arrival month, meal plan, and market segment."}
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(7, 4, 3, 1))

boxplot(model_residuals ~ model_data$arrival_date_month,
        names = month.abb, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7,
        xlab = "Arrival month", ylab = "Residual",
        main = "Residuals by month")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

boxplot(model_residuals ~ model_data$meal,
        las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7,
        xlab = "Meal", ylab = "Residual",
        main = "Residuals by meal")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

boxplot(model_residuals ~ model_data$market_segment,
        las = 2, cex.axis = 0.6,
        xlab = "Market segment", ylab = "Residual",
        main = "Residuals by market segment")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

par(old_par)
```

```{r residual-categorical-2, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap="Residuals by customer type and reserved room type."}
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(7, 4, 3, 1))

boxplot(model_residuals ~ model_data$customer_type,
        las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7,
        xlab = "Customer type", ylab = "Residual",
        main = "Residuals by customer type")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

boxplot(model_residuals ~ model_data$reserved_room_type,
        las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7,
        xlab = "Reserved room type", ylab = "Residual",
        main = "Residuals by room type")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

par(old_par)
```

```{r residual-categorical-3, fig.width=10, fig.height=4, fig.cap="Residuals by repeat-guest and domestic status."}
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))

boxplot(model_residuals ~ model_data$is_repeated_guest,
        xlab = "Repeat guest", ylab = "Residual",
        main = "Residuals by repeat-guest status")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

boxplot(model_residuals ~ model_data$domestic,
        xlab = "Domestic status", ylab = "Residual",
        main = "Residuals by domestic status")
abline(h = 0, col = "red")

par(old_par)
```

The residuals-versus-fitted and residuals-versus-lead-time plots show systematic patterns and changing spread. Therefore, the linearity and constant variance assumptions are questionable. The residual plots for the remaining predictors are generally centered near zero, although several discrete predictors form bands and some categories have different spreads. The normal Q-Q plot shows substantial departures from the reference line in both tails, so the normality assumption is not reasonable. Group bookings or repeat guests may produce related errors, but the available data do not contain enough identifying information to verify the uncorrelated-errors assumption. Following the Part 1 instructions, we identify these violations without correcting them in the preliminary model.
